title: One Porsche Racing Driver Walked Away From a Violent Crash at One of Europe's Most Historic Circuits, Just One of Several Wild Wrecks That Rattled an Entire Motorsport Weekend - NewsBreak
text:
By Shaun Hastings ,
21 hours ago One Porsche Racing Driver Walked Away From a Violent Crash at One of Europe's Most Historic Circuits, Just One of Several Wild Wrecks That Rattled an Entire Motorsport Weekend Porsche Supercup driver Sam Shahin walked away unhurt after a violent, full-speed collision sent his car spinning into the gravel trap at Monza’s Ascari chicane, one of several wild wrecks that rattled the historic circuit during a chaotic Formula 1 weekend.
Photo by redcharlie on Unsplash A Crash at Full Speed Shahin was hit by Andrea Galli on just the second lap of the race, contact that sent his car off into the gravel according to a motorsport wire report on the weekend’s crashes. Shahin described the moment afterward, writing that a “reckless driver ignored multiple flag warning signals and multiple Safety Car signals” before barreling “into yours truly at full speed.” Both drivers were able to walk away from the wreck. It was not the only chaos of the day: earlier in the same lap, three cars collided within seconds of each other at a separate chicane, and another driver, Caleb Sumich, was hit into the gravel elsewhere on the circuit.
Race Cut Short According to Porsche’s own race report , officials red-flagged the race so marshals could clear the wreckage and repair damaged guardrails. Track crews could not finish the work inside the allotted window, so the race was never restarted, and the final classification reverted to the running order from the first lap. Andrea Bristot of Dinamic Motorsport was declared the winner, his first Supercup victory. “This is not how I wanted to celebrate my first Supercup victory,” Bristot said afterward, according to the official report. “But these things are beyond our control in motor racing.”
A Rough Weekend Across the Board Despite the carnage, the Supercup championship was still decided at Monza. Flynt Schuring, 20, clinched the overall title as the series’ youngest champion since 1993, while Chester Kieffer won the rookie crown and Schumacher CLRT secured its third consecutive teams’ championship.
Monza’s layout, with its high-speed chicanes designed decades before modern safety barriers became standard, continues to test both driver skill and race control’s ability to manage incidents quickly. The circuit’s history of dramatic crashes across multiple racing series has made it one of the more closely studied tracks in motorsport safety circles, and weekends like this one, with wrecks spread across several different support races on top of Formula 1’s own headline event, tend to reignite discussion about whether additional runoff area or barrier upgrades are needed at specific corners.
Formula 1’s own presence at Monza that same weekend added extra scrutiny to every support race running on the same circuit, since a red flag or safety concern during a support series can eat into the schedule buffer built around the headline event. Race organizers at historic circuits like Monza increasingly have to balance preserving a track’s traditional, high-speed character against modern safety expectations, a tension that shows up clearly whenever a weekend produces this many incidents across multiple series running the same layout within a matter of hours.
